cards.text: In those days, there was no king in Israel. A Levite living way out in the remote hill country of Ephraim takes a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah. Friend, I'll be straight with you: this is one of the hardest stories in the whole Bible, so stay close to me on this one.

cards.question: The Levite's concubine is unfaithful to him and leaves him. Where does she go?

answers.text: Her father's house in Bethlehem
The house of the LORD in Shiloh
Her sister's house in Hebron

cards.text: She's been there four months. Then her husband gets up and goes after her, taking his servant and a pair of donkeys.

cards.question: The Levite travels all the way to Bethlehem after his concubine. What does he go there to do?

answers.text: Speak kindly to her and bring her back
Demand payment from her father
Bring her before the town elders

cards.question: The girl brings the Levite into her father's house. True or false: her father is unhappy to see him.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: He gladly welcomes him and persuades him to stay. So the Levite stays three days, eating, drinking and lodging there.

cards.question: On the fourth day, the Levite is up early and ready to leave. What does the girl's father tell him first?

answers.text: Have a bite of bread before you go
The roads are too dangerous today
My daughter is not ready to leave

cards.text: So the two of them sit down and eat and drink together. Then the father asks him to stay the night, and when the man gets up to go, his father-in-law talks him into it.

cards.question: On the fifth day, the Levite gets up early to leave. True or false: he's on the road by morning.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: They wait until late afternoon and eat again, and then the father says the day's almost over, so please spend the night. Friend, this man is getting SNOOZED by his father-in-law, and every time he stands up, BOOP, five more minutes.

cards.question: The father-in-law begs the Levite to spend the night one more time. What does the Levite do?

answers.text: Leaves anyway with his concubine
Asks to stay a whole week
Sends his servant home alone

cards.text: He finally IGNORES the snooze button, and off they go with the two saddled donkeys. They come near Jebus, that's Jerusalem, and the day is almost gone.

cards.question: It's getting dark near Jebus. What does the Levite's servant suggest?

answers.text: Stop and spend the night in Jebus
Turn back to the house in Bethlehem
Keep walking all through the night

cards.question: The Levite says no to stopping in Jebus. Why?

answers.text: It is a city of foreigners with no Israelites
Its gates are already shut for the night
He has made enemies who live there

cards.text: They push on, hoping to reach Gibeah or Ramah, and the sun sets as they near Gibeah in Benjamin. They turn in to lodge there, and the Levite sits down in the city square.

cards.question: The Levite and his group are sitting in Gibeah's city square at nightfall. True or false: someone quickly takes them into his home.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: That evening, an old man comes in from his work in the field. He's from the hill country of Ephraim too, living here in Gibeah, where the men are Benjamites.

cards.question: The old man looks up and sees the traveler in the city square. What does he ask him?

answers.text: Where he is going and where he came from
Whether he can pay for a room tonight
Why he brought his donkeys into town

cards.text: The Levite tells him they're traveling from Bethlehem in Judah, headed home to the hill country of Ephraim. He says he's going to the house of the LORD, but no one has taken him into his home.

cards.question: No one in Gibeah has taken the Levite in. What does he tell the old man about their supplies?

answers.text: They already have everything they need
They have run out of bread and wine
Their donkeys have not eaten all day

cards.question: The old man says, "Peace to you," and offers to supply everything the Levite needs. What's the one thing he tells him not to do?

answers.text: Spend the night in the square
Tell anyone where he is from
Leave the house before morning

cards.text: So he brings them home and feeds the donkeys, and they wash their feet and eat and drink. Finally, friend, a door opens.
But while they're enjoying themselves, the wicked men of the city suddenly surround the house. They start pounding on the door.

cards.question: The wicked men of Gibeah pound on the old man's door. They demand he bring someone out so they can have relations with him. Who?

answers.text: The Levite staying as his guest
The women staying in the house
The old man's own sons

cards.text: The old man goes out and says, "No, my brothers, do not do this wicked thing!" He reminds them this man is a guest in his house.

cards.question: True or false: the old man offers to bring out his own virgin daughter and the Levite's concubine instead.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: But the men won't listen to him. So the Levite takes his concubine and sends her outside to them.
They rape her and abuse her throughout the night.

cards.question: At dawn, the men let the concubine go. Where does she go?

answers.text: Back to the house where her master is staying
Back to her father's house in Bethlehem
Out to the gate of the city

cards.text: She collapses at the doorway and lies there until it's light. In the morning, her master opens the doors to go on his journey, and there she is, with her hands on the threshold.

cards.question: The Levite finds his concubine collapsed in the doorway. What does he say to her?

answers.text: Get up and let us go
Forgive me for what I did
Wait here while I find help

cards.text: But there's no response, so he puts her on his donkey and sets out for home. When he gets there, he takes a knife and cuts her limb by limb into twelve pieces.

cards.question: The Levite cuts his concubine's body into twelve pieces. Where does he send them?

answers.text: Throughout the territory of Israel
To the elders of Gibeah
To her father in Bethlehem

cards.question: Everyone who sees the pieces of the concubine's body says nothing like this has been seen or done since when?

answers.text: The day Israel came out of Egypt
The days of the great flood
The day Joshua crossed the Jordan

cards.question: Everyone who sees the pieces of the concubine's body also gives a call to action. What do they say to do?

answers.text: Think it over and speak up
March on Gibeah right away
Send word back to Bethlehem

cards.text: I'm going to close the oven door here for a minute, friend. This story isn't finished, and neither are we.

findings.problem: This is a where question, but 'Her sister's house in Hebron' invents a sister and a destination instead of using a real detail from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish. Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: Nine of the ten choice cards are multiple choice, while only one is true or false. Multiple choice therefore dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Too many choices depend on discovering an unforeseeable detail rather than reasoning from earlier cards. Cards 4, 8, 10, 17, 18 and 19 provide no earlier basis for inferring the supplies, the mob's target, the old man's offer, where the pieces are sent, the starting point of the comparison or the call to action. Six discovery questions out of ten are more than the allowed few.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: This is a who question, but 'The old man's own sons' invents people who are not a real detail from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish. Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: This is a where question, but 'To the elders of Gibeah' is an invented destination rather than a real detail from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish. Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.
